author: Hodgson, 1837
summary: 우리나라에서는 제주도 서귀포 부근에서 드물게 기록되는 길잃은새이다. 해안 절벽과 동굴, 바위섬에 살며 트인 곳에서 번식한다. 국외에서는 아프리카와 중국, 타이완, 필리핀 등 동남아시아에 분포한다.

art.subject: House Swift (Apus nipalensis), adult, as seen over the southern Jeju coast in summer: plumage sooty black overall, slightly glossed above; a broad, square-cut white band across the rump that wraps slightly onto the rear flanks; a contrasting whitish throat patch; wings blackish; tail short and black, square-ended or very slightly notched; tiny black bill; dark eye.
art.pose: flying fast along a sea cliff
art.scene: Korean southern coast of Jeju near Seogwipo in summer: sea cliffs, caves and rocky islets; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, in flight seen from above, head, body and tail in line: sooty black back and wings, broad white rump band, short square-ended tail with only a slight notch
adult, in flight seen from below: blackish body and underwings, contrasting whitish throat, short square tail
art.build: Small, stocky swift, about 13cm, roughly sparrow length, with long, scythe-shaped wings that are shorter and broader than Pacific Swift's and a short, square or barely notched tail. Head broad and rounded, bill tiny with a wide gape, feet tiny and never used for perching on wires. Flight fast with rapid flickering wingbeats and glides, often in groups around cliffs.
avoid: Do not paint a long, deeply forked tail, a narrow white rump band or pale scaling on the underparts; those belong to Pacific Swift (Apus pacificus).
Do not paint a white back; only the rump band is white.
Do not paint a red throat, white belly or long tail streamers; that is Barn Swallow.
Do not show it perched on a wire or branch.
